extracted.intended_audience: researchers, students, and practitioners interested in news consumption, news sharing, and computational communication methods
extracted.subtask_short: research on news consumption and dissemination
extracted.subtask_description: Describes research questions and methods about how citizens keep up with and engage with news, and how journalists, news media, social media, and technical innovations shape that process; emphasizes survey and digital-trace methods, computational techniques, and experimental tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: News consumption and sources
rubrics_metrics.description: What types of news are people using – and whom? Do people still watch television news, and what role do online media play?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically investigated with survey research (early career); nowadays typically investigated with digital trace data, for example so‑called data donations, in which people donate their browser histories for scientific research. This line of research includes news of all kinds of news-related information, including low- and high-quality news, opinionated and factual content, and even mis- and disinformation. (Original wording: 'What types of news are people using – and whom? Do people still watch television news, and what role do online media play?... Nowadays, I typically use digital trace data, for example so-called data donations... This line of research includes news of all kind of news-related information, including low- and high-quality news, opinionated and factual content, and even mis- and disinformation.')

rubrics_metrics.name: News sharing and shareworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding what makes news 'shareworthy' and the dynamics of news sharing across platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate predictors of sharing based on article characteristics and perform large-scale analyses of news sharing (example: Facebook). (Original wording: 'Furthermore, I have worked extensively on news sharing. This includes understanding what makes news “shareworthy” and large-scale analyses of news sharing on Facebook.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Human and algorithmic feedback loops in news production and dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for reinforcing processes where content becomes popular because it's already popular, personalized news diets based on earlier clicks, and the influence of audience metrics on content production and dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research should explicitly consider feedback loops between human behavior and algorithms (popularity bias, personalization, editorial responses to metrics). The page notes that the term 'filter bubble' is often used in such contexts but may be misleading; links to the NEWSFLOWS project for further work. (Original wording: 'News sharing and news consumption in today’s media environment cannot be understood without considering re-inforcing processes: content that becomes popular just because it is already popular; increasingly personalized news diets based on earlier clicks; the influence of audience metrics on content production and dissemination.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Application and development of computational methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and develop innovative computational methods and tools for studying news and communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of valued methods: state-of-the-art machine learning techniques; methods to identify news events and trace them across media; tools for field experiments with recommender systems; and tools for data donation. The author is involved in editorial work for a computational communication journal and co-authored a practical methods book. (Original wording: 'One of my main interests is the application and development of innovative methods... I am one of the founding associate editors of the diamond open-access journal Computational Communication Research... Also, I co-authored a book on Computational Analysis of Communication... Amongst other things, I am interested in the use of state-of-the art machine learning techniques, developing methods to identify news events and to trace them between different types of media, developing tools for field experiments with recommender systems and for data donation.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and promotion of open-source/data-donation frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt or develop open-source frameworks to collect and enable analysis of digital-trace data (data donation) ethically and reproducibly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page references concrete work on data-donation frameworks (example: OSD2F: an open-source data donation framework) and highlights data donation as a primary methodological approach for contemporary news-consumption research. Emphasis on tool development and sharing to support reproducible computational communication research. (Original wording: 'Nowadays, I typically use digital trace data, for example so-called data donations... Osd2f: an open-source data donation framework.')
